subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary or appears in fallbacks?
rationale: This adds a public config knob and changes provider routing/fallback semantics across model resolution, auth visibility, and status output, so source inspection can prove the gap but cannot choose the intended user-facing behavior.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, models.json planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current operator model where users remove provider blocks or edit fallback lists, avoiding another public config surface and its routing semantics.

options.title: Defer to provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until provider enable/disable, plugin setup, auth/status, model picker, and fallback behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, models.json planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests, including disabled-primary semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central model/provider config paths and prior issue review both point to steipete as the best available owner for the shared config and routing decision.
